overall_explanation:
I inspected the supplied current-source dataset (btw.ts, compact.ts, extensions.ts, run.ts, run/attempt.ts, stream-resolution.ts, sessions/extensions/runner.ts, context-final-snapshot.ts, context-orchestrator.ts, rc03-producers.ts, rc03-seal-hook.ts, seal-registry.ts, context-candidate.ts, kill-switch config source, extension runner, compaction core, and the three new/updated test suites) rather than relying on the change summary.

What checks out:
- Default-off is preserved: RC-03 resolution stays opt-in (`OPENCLAW_RC03_SEAL=1` or `runtime.rc03.seal=true`) and the enhancement kill switch wins; off paths report `sealCoverage=disabled`, persist no plan/receipt, and the request bytes are unchanged (the only new default-path work is a cached config stat plus a no-op plan clear).
- Creation and enforcement now resolve the same current configuration (`resolveCurrentRc03SealState`), and the historical turn-kill lineage is no longer used as the current enforcement decision.
- Producer/phase facts are derived from one registry: registrations are frozen copies, the coverage matrix is a derived read-only projection, plan readbacks are structured clones, and pre-seal/post-seal admission goes through `assertSealMutation`. Unknown applied lineage sources now reach admission instead of being dropped, and the two newly registered producers (`session-start-injection`, `btw-side-question`) are mapped from real lineage ids.
- Model-call identity is shared: the context producer advances via `nextRc03ModelCallIndex`, the stream wrapper consumes the same sequence (summarizer takes its own index, denied calls do not advance the counter), explicit summary identities are reused rather than renamed, and the sealed digest is always bound (including the empty prompt) with the cache-boundary marker stripped consistently on both sides.
- The context callback now binds the live session prompt (`ctx.getSystemPrompt()`), which covers continuations that skip `before_agent_start`; the effective prompt is hashed even when empty.
- Temporary clearing (`clearRc03SealPlan`) is separated from end-of-run release (`releaseRc03Run`/`endRc03RunAttempts`), BTW seals under an ephemeral run identity and releases it in `finally`, and standalone manual compaction falls back to the session identity and releases only the state it owns.
- Seal denial is propagated structurally through the extension runner (`SealMutationError` rethrown) while ordinary optional extension failures stay fail-open.
- Docs, harness rule, task-spec wiring, flag catalog and artifact manifest are updated consistently with the code; the matrix has 18 registered rows and the frozen default-off/6000-char/product locks are untouched.

Residual risk I noted but did not treat as an actionable defect because I could not show a reachable production break and it is deliberate fail-closed design under an opt-in flag: `sealBoundaryModelCall` now throws `unsealed-model-call` for any non-summarizer call that has no sealed plan (previously it recorded a census failure and continued), so a hypothetical model call that bypasses the orchestrator seal would abort the turn rather than run unverified. The remaining known gaps in the bundle (two pre-existing COMPASS/budget failures in the broad suite, a handoff failure under diagnosis, and the absence of live-provider/adapter-wire attestation) are already stated as unproven boundaries rather than claimed results.
